name: ABNT NBR 9050 (accessible route)
checked: Checked against the text of ABNT NBR 9050:2020 by a contributor (pull request #386).
note: For a stair on an accessible route. An emergency exit is held to NBR 9077 instead (the next entry), and in most states to the fire brigade's own instruction, which rules over it (São Paulo's IT 11, Santa Catarina's IN 09). Curved and mixed flights are allowed when the tread and riser on the walk line keep to 6.8.2. Headroom and the most risers in a flight are not in the standard: forgiving numbers. Risers within a flight are constant; 0.5 mm is the tolerance used for that.

sources.stairs.riser: NBR 9050:2020 6.8.2, a riser in its range
sources.stairs.going: NBR 9050:2020 6.8.2, a tread in its range
sources.stairs.headroom: Not in the standard: a forgiving number (2.10 m is the standard's height for doors and passages)
sources.stairs.flight_rise_max: NBR 9050:2020 6.8.7, a landing every 3.20 m of rise
sources.stairs.flight_risers_max: Not in the standard: a forgiving number (3.20 m ÷ 160 mm)
sources.stairs.winders: NBR 9050:2020 6.8.6, curved or mixed flights keeping 6.8.2 on the walk line
sources.stairs.walk_line_offset: NBR 9050:2020 6.8.6, 0.55 m from the inner edge
sources.stairs.open_risers: NBR 9050:2020 6.8.4, no open risers on an accessible route
sources.stairs.handrail_min: NBR 9050:2020 6.9.3.2, the lower rail at 0.70 m
sources.stairs.handrail_max: NBR 9050:2020 6.9.3.2, the upper rail at 0.92 m
sources.stairs.guard_min: NBR 9077:2001 4.8.1.2, 1.05 m as the general rule
